results: Requirement F17 fully implemented: Shadow decision never changes enforced result and divergence is auditable.
Thread-safe shadow evaluation engine implemented in internal/rollout/shadow.go with bounded MemoryDivergenceStore.

Strict non-interference verified: authoritative decision (allow, status code, obligations) is 100% governed by enforced policy under all conditions including candidate denials, candidate permits, candidate panics, and candidate timeouts.

Resilient candidate isolation verified: candidate evaluation panics, timeout bounds, and syntax faults are safely trapped and recorded as SHADOW_ERROR without impacting the enforced authorization decision.

GDPR-aligned zero-token auditing verified: divergence records contain deterministic HMAC-SHA256 subject pseudonyms and fully redacted credentials; no Bearer tokens, raw JWTs, or session cookies appear in serialized records.
Private resources fail closed: unauthenticated requests to private resources strictly fail closed (403 Forbidden) on enforced evaluation regardless of candidate policy.
Explicit negative error semantics verified: missing required prerequisites return HTTP 400 MALFORMED_REQUEST; unavailable providers return HTTP 503 PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE.
Restart invariance verified: divergence store state exports and imports with 100% fidelity across engine restarts preserving records, order, and aggregate metrics.

CLI -evaluate-shadow flag and live HTTP endpoints (/api/v1/rollout/shadow/evaluate, /v1/runtime/rollout/shadow, /api/v1/rollout/shadow/divergence) registered in cmd/policyhelix/main.go and proxied through Node supervisor (scripts/serve-web.mjs).
Eight Apache-2.0 synthetic fixtures cataloged with SHA-256 digests in tests/fixtures/policyhelix/C23/manifest.json.

Automated regression test coverage established in tests/shadow_test.go covering manifest integrity, acceptance non-interference, credential redaction, panic isolation, fail-closed semantics, CLI execution, and HTTP endpoints.
